based_in.value: Manama, Bahrain, with operations in Saudi Arabia and the UAE

growth_signal.value: Live and regulated in three countries; Saudi banks are now investing in it and it acquired an AI company, Servable

raised.value: $50M strategic financing in September 2026 from Riyad Bank, SAB Invest's X-Tech Fund, GIB and others, after a $13M seed years earlier

entry.idea: Runs the regulated pipes that let apps and banks in the Gulf read a customer's bank data and move money with their consent, the way open banking works in Europe.
entry.lesson: Be the first to go through a new regulation with the regulator; the rulebook you help write becomes your moat.
entry.name: Tarabut

growth.basis: substitute: funding round bigger than the last, acquisition
growth.reason: No customer or volume numbers published; the signal is banks putting $50M in and a fresh acquisition.

market.reason: Every bank and fintech in the Gulf will need these pipes, but the region is a few rich countries rather than the whole world.

tech.reason: The software is standard open-banking plumbing; the licences in three countries are what is hard to copy.

sources.title: Tarabut secures $50 million to deepen Saudi embedded finance push (Wamda)
Tarabut: From a Bahrain Sandbox to GCC-wide Open Finance (StartUp Bahrain)

entry.twist: It was the first company through Bahrain's regulatory sandbox in 2018, so it wrote the template regulators in Saudi Arabia and the UAE later followed.
entry.who_pays: Banks, fintechs and large companies pay to connect through the platform.
entry.why_now: Gulf regulators are mandating open banking and Saudi banks want embedded finance without building it themselves.

mentions.snippet: Open banking and embedded finance infrastructure; $50M strategic financing for Saudi push.
